characters.name: Mira
characters.description: Organized, calm, enjoys planning and making lists. Under pressure, she clings tightly to order.

characters.name: Theo
characters.description: Practical, friendly, good at carrying supplies and fixing small setup issues. He jokes when uneasy.

characters.name: Hana
characters.description: Thoughtful, artistic, pays attention to colors and small details. She notices small things others miss.

locations.description: Quiet afternoon entrance beneath a low cloudy sky, with thin foot traffic and a lingering sense of being watched.
Clean hallway with windows, a wall clock, bulletin boards, and a simple wall pattern that seems too regular in the dim light.
Tables, art supplies, a notebook, posters, tape, and folders, all arranged as if someone had touched them recently.
Shelves, cardboard boxes, frames, folded stands, an old radio, and a photograph on a shelf, the air dry and stale.
Unused classroom prepared for a small exhibition, desks pushed aside, wide windows, and a silence that collects in the corners.
Benches, small plants, calm outdoor space, with light rain later in the story and reflections that look darker than they should.

narration: The school day had ended, and the front gate was almost empty.
A few soft clouds covered the sky, but the light felt thin and colorless.
Mira stood near the gate with a canvas tote bag over one shoulder.
Inside were folders, tape, and a carefully written checklist.
She looked at the school building and smiled in a small, satisfied way.
The windows reflected the sky.
For a moment, they looked like dull eyes.
Theo arrived next, carrying a folded poster tube under one arm.
Hana walked up soon after, holding a flat folder against her chest.
The three of them were preparing a small art exhibition for the next day.
It was not a large event, only a simple display of student sketches, watercolor studies, and photographs.
Still, they wanted the room to look neat.
The words sounded harmless.
Together, they walked through the gate and into the school.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: I brought the extra posters. I checked twice this morning.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Good. That saves us a trip later.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: I brought the title cards. They’re simple, but I think they match the exhibition.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Perfect. If we work steadily, we should finish before it gets late.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Art club room first?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Yes. We’ll check the supplies, then move everything to the old classroom.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Let’s make it a quiet, tidy kind of exhibition.

actions: Mira waits near the school gate with her tote bag.
Theo arrives carrying a folded poster tube.
Hana arrives holding her folder.
The group enters the school together.

narration: The hallway was clean and still.
Afternoon light came through the windows, forming pale rectangles on the floor.
A wall clock ticked steadily above a bulletin board covered with event notices.
The ticking seemed too loud for an empty school.
Mira opened her tote bag and pulled out a notebook.
The cover was plain blue, with a small paper label that read “Exhibition Plan.”
They passed the windows.
Outside, the courtyard plants moved slightly in the wind.
Inside, nothing moved except them.
The school felt ordinary and familiar after classes.
But the sound of their footsteps seemed to come back half a step late.
Theo looked at the wall clock.
The clock ticked again.
They reached the art club room door and went inside.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: I made a list: frames, stands, labels, tape, cloth, and the visitor comment sheet.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: And snacks?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Not on this list.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Maybe next time.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: We have about three hours before the building closes.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: That should be enough.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: If we don’t spend twenty minutes deciding where every drawing goes.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: We might spend ten.

actions: Mira takes out the blue exhibition notebook.
The group walks through the quiet hallway.
Theo checks the wall clock.
They enter the art club room.

narration: The art club room held several long tables.
Rolls of tape, brushes, paper scraps, and folders were arranged in small piles.
A few finished posters leaned against the wall.
Everything looked normal.
Everything looked a little too ready.
Mira placed the blue notebook on the table.
Theo set down the poster tube.
Hana opened her folder and carefully removed the title cards.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Before we move anything, we should confirm what we have.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Should we start with the notebook or the schedule?

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Either is fine. We just need a starting point.

actions: The group prepares to check the supplies.
Mira places the exhibition notebook on the table.
Hana arranges the title cards carefully.

choices.text: Check the wall clock and schedule first.

narration: Mira opened the notebook to the first marked page.
The list was written neatly, with small boxes beside each item.
The handwriting was hers.
Still, she paused before reading.
Hana pointed to the next page.
Hana studied the lines.
Mira looked down.
There was only a small smudge near the edge of the page.
The group agreed to use the notebook as their guide.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Frames: eight. Stands: four. Labels: one sheet. Tape: two rolls. Cloth: one folded piece.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: That’s clear enough. We can check items as we find them.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: You even drew a room layout.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: A rough one. We can adjust it later.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Did you draw that mark by the windows?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Probably pencil dust.

actions: Mira reads from the supply list.
Hana notices a small smudge near the window mark in the layout.
They decide to follow the notebook.

narration: Theo looked up at the clock near the door and compared it with the note on Mira’s schedule.
The second hand twitched forward.
Then paused.
Then moved again.
Hana placed the title cards in a neat row.
Theo kept looking at the clock for one more second.
They agreed to follow a simple schedule and keep moving at a steady pace.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: If we spend thirty minutes here, one hour moving and arranging, then the rest on labels and cleanup, we’ll be fine.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: That sounds reasonable.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Then we should not overthink the first part.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Right. Simple schedule.

actions: Theo compares the wall clock with Mira’s schedule.
The clock hand briefly pauses before moving again.
The group commits to a steady schedule.

narration: With their first step decided, the three began checking supplies.
Mira marked items on the list.
Theo tested two tape rolls to make sure they still worked.
Hana checked that the title cards were clean and flat.
For a while, everything seemed to be where it belonged.
Then Mira paused.
Hana looked around the supplies.
Theo lifted the poster tube.
Mira did not look worried.
But her fingers tightened around the pen.
They gathered what they had and prepared to visit the storage room.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: The label sheet should be here, but I don’t see it on the table.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: It might be inside one of the folders.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Or packed with the frames.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: It’s probably nearby. We can continue and find it as we go.

actions: The group checks the art supplies.
Mira notices the printed label sheet is missing.
They decide to continue and look for it later.

narration: The group sorted the remaining items into three piles.
There were items to carry now, items to carry later, and items to leave behind.
Theo lifted a folded cloth from a chair.
Dust slipped from the fabric in a gray breath.
Hana examined it.
She brushed the cloth once.
The dust left a dark streak on her fingertips.
Mira placed a check mark beside “cloth” in the notebook.
The missing label sheet was still not visible.
It should have been a small issue.
They had blank cards if needed.
Hana’s handwriting was neat enough to make replacements.
Still, using the printed labels would be easier.
As they left, one of the posters shifted against the wall.
It settled before anyone could say anything.
They walked down the hallway.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: This can cover the front table.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: The color is simple. It won’t distract from the artwork.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: We’ll keep an eye out. For now, frames and stands.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Storage room trip.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: I’ll keep these with me so they don’t get bent.

actions: The group sorts supplies into piles.
Theo lifts the folded cloth.
Hana puts the title cards back into her folder.
A poster shifts against the wall as they leave.

narration: The storage room was small but orderly.
Shelves lined the walls, holding cardboard boxes, spare paper, folded display stands, and old decorations from past events.
The air was dry.
It smelled like paper, dust, and something faintly metallic.
A small radio sat on one shelf beside a framed photograph of a previous school festival.
Theo turned on the ceiling light.
The bulb flickered twice before staying on.
Hana looked at the photograph on the shelf.
It showed a classroom decorated with paper flowers and drawings.
The students in the picture were blurred by glare.
Theo carefully pulled out the frames one by one.
Hana found a roll of extra tape and placed it in the carrying box.
The old radio had a small label on it that said “Works sometimes.”
Theo gave it a curious look but left it alone.
A thin static sound came from it.
Theo froze.
The radio dial was set to off.
His voice stayed light.
The static faded.
They carried the frames, stands, and tape out of the storage room and toward the old classroom.
No one turned off the light behind them.
It flickered anyway.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Frames are on the second shelf.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Eight frames.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: This room has stored a lot of school projects.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: That’s a nice way to put it.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: One, two, three… eight. All here.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Display stands are here too.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: This might help if the posters curl.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: We probably don’t need background music.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Maybe during setup, but not during the exhibition.

actions: Theo turns on the storage room light.
The group collects eight frames, display stands, and extra tape.
The old radio emits static while switched off.
They leave the storage room with the supplies.

narration: The old classroom was not used for regular lessons anymore, but it was clean and bright.
The desks had been stacked along one side.
The windows gave the room soft natural light.
A simple wall pattern ran beneath the chalkboard.
The room felt larger than it should.
Mira set the notebook on the front desk.
Hana laid the title cards beside it.
Theo leaned the frames against the wall.
They considered the room quietly.
The old classroom considered them back.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: So, where do we start?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Tables first, then wall display.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Or wall display first, then tables.

actions: The group enters the old classroom gallery.
Mira sets down the notebook.
Hana places the title cards beside it.
Theo leans the frames against the wall.

choices.text: Ask Mira about the table arrangement.
Ask Hana about the wall display.

narration: Theo turned to Mira.
Mira looked at her rough layout.
Hana looked across the room.
The middle of the room looked too open.
Theo nodded.
Mira kept her eyes on the notebook.
They began with the tables.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: How do you want the tables?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: One table near the entrance for the comment sheet, and two along the side for smaller works.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: That keeps the middle open.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Easy to walk through.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Yes. Easy.

actions: Theo asks Mira about the table arrangement.
Mira explains the layout from her notebook.
The group begins by arranging the tables.

narration: Mira turned to Hana.
Hana stood back and studied the blank wall.
The blank wall seemed to absorb her voice.
Theo lifted one frame slightly.
Mira wrote a quick note in the margin of her layout.
Hana touched one of the title cards.
They began with the wall spacing.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: What do you think about the wall display?

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: The larger watercolor pieces should go in the center. Smaller sketches can go around them.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Balanced but not crowded.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Good. Let’s use that.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: The center should feel calm.

actions: Mira asks Hana about the wall display.
Hana studies the blank wall.
Mira notes Hana’s suggestion in the layout.
The group begins spacing the wall display.

narration: After a few minutes, the arrangement became clear.
Tables would stay along the sides, and the central wall would hold the largest pieces.
Smaller works would fill the space around them.
The room looked simple, open, and easy to walk through.
Hana said it as if she were convincing herself.
Mira smiled faintly.
The wide windows reflected the three of them.
For an instant, the reflections looked slightly out of order.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: This already feels better.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: It feels like a room that knows what it’s doing.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: That is the goal.

actions: The table and wall display plan becomes clear.
The group observes the room taking shape.
The window reflections briefly appear out of order.

narration: They worked steadily.
Theo unfolded the display stands and checked that each one stood straight.
Mira placed frames on the tables in the order written in the notebook.
Hana adjusted the spacing between artworks.
She stepped back every few minutes to compare the distance.
The wall clock in the hallway could be heard faintly whenever the classroom door was open.
Its sound was ordinary.
Tick.
Tick.
Tick.
Too patient.
Mira taped the first title card beneath a watercolor study.
Theo placed the folded cloth over the front table.
Theo searched the supply box and pulled out two pens.
Hana’s smile faded when she looked at the central watercolor.
It was only a study of trees near a river.
But in the gray afternoon light, the spaces between the trunks looked like standing figures.
The missing label sheet had still not appeared.
Mira made a note to check the notebook pocket later.
For now, the room was taking shape.
The more complete it became, the less empty it felt.
That should have been comforting.
It was not.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Straight?

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: A little to the left.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Now it’s straight.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Comment sheet goes here?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Yes. Along with a pen.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: One main pen, one backup pen.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Very official.

actions: Theo unfolds and checks the display stands.
Mira arranges frames according to the notebook.
Hana adjusts artwork spacing.
Mira attaches the first title card.
Theo places the cloth and pens on the front table.
Hana notices the tree shapes in the central watercolor.

narration: After an hour of arranging, they decided to step outside for a short break.
The courtyard garden was quiet.
A few benches sat between small plants, and the air smelled clean.
Light rain began to fall.
It was soft enough that they could remain under the covered walkway without getting wet.
Mira sat on the bench and closed the notebook over her lap.
Raindrops made small circles in a shallow puddle near the plants.
The sound was even and calm.
The puddle reflected the school windows.
The old classroom window looked black.
Hana looked toward it.
A pause followed.
Mira checked the time.
They rested quietly for a moment, watching the ordinary rhythm of the rain.
Behind them, somewhere inside, the hallway clock kept ticking.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Carrying frames counts as exercise.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Arranging frames counts as patience.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: We are doing fine.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: The rain makes the light softer. The room might look nice this way.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Good exhibition weather.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: For quiet people.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: We still have enough time for labels and cleanup.

actions: The group takes a short break in the courtyard garden.
Light rain begins.
Hana looks toward the old classroom window.
Mira checks the time.

narration: The break had been short, but useful.
The group had to decide how to spend the next few minutes.
The rain tapped softly on the covered walkway.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Should we go back now, or take five more minutes?

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Either works.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: As long as we finish the labels.

actions: The group considers whether to return immediately or rest a little longer.

choices.text: Take five more minutes before returning.

narration: Mira stood and tucked the notebook under her arm.
Theo picked up the extra tape.
Hana brushed a few raindrops from her sleeve.
She looked once at the dark classroom window.
They returned to the old classroom.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Let’s finish while we still have energy.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Good plan.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: I want to see the whole display finished.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: All of it.

actions: Mira stands with the notebook.
Theo picks up the tape.
Hana glances at the old classroom window.
The group returns inside.

narration: They stayed under the covered walkway a little longer.
Theo leaned back against the bench and listened to the rain.
Hana looked at the plants.
Mira glanced at the notebook but did not open it.
The five minutes passed slowly.
When they stood, the bench behind them was dry except for three dark marks where they had been sitting.
After the short pause, they returned to the old classroom.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Five minutes is enough to feel like a real break.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: The leaves look brighter after rain starts.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: All right. Five minutes, then labels.

actions: The group rests for five more minutes.
They notice three dark marks on the bench after standing.
They return to the old classroom.

narration: The old classroom looked calm when they came back.
The windows showed the gray afternoon sky.
The artwork stood neatly in place.
Nothing had fallen.
Nothing had moved.
Mira opened the notebook again.
Theo placed the pens on the front table.
Hana lined up the remaining title cards.
The room waited.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Final tasks: labels, comment sheet, and cleanup.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Ready.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Let’s finish.

actions: The group returns to the old classroom gallery.
Mira opens the notebook.
Theo places the pens on the table.
Hana lines up the remaining title cards.

narration: They began attaching the last title cards.
Hana wrote two small replacement labels by hand, just in case the printed sheet did not turn up.
Her handwriting was clear and even.
Mira flipped through the notebook to compare the artwork order.
Page after page.
Frames.
Stands.
Labels.
Tape.
Cloth.
Visitor comment sheet.
As she turned to the back cover, a folded paper slipped out of the inside pocket and landed on the desk.
Theo noticed it first.
Mira unfolded it.
She stared at it a little too long.
The printed labels matched the artwork list, so they replaced the temporary handwritten ones.
Hana kept the handwritten cards in the folder as spares.
Theo walked around the room and checked the tape.
Mira placed the comment sheet on the front table and set the backup pen beside it.
Hana stood near the entrance and looked over the room.
The exhibition was ready.
Mira glanced down at the folded label sheet again.
For a moment, she thought there were too many labels.
Then she counted them.
Everything matched.
Everything was fine.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Is that the label sheet?

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Yes. I put it in the pocket so it wouldn’t bend.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: That is a very organized way to misplace something.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Accurate.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Nothing is loose.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Everything on the list is done.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: It feels simple, but complete.

actions: Hana writes two temporary replacement labels.
Mira flips through the notebook.
The missing label sheet falls from the notebook pocket.
The group replaces the handwritten labels with the printed ones.
Theo checks the tape around the room.
Mira places the comment sheet and backup pen on the front table.

narration: A short preview was held before the building closed.
A few visitors passed through quietly, looking at the artwork and reading the labels.
No one stayed long.
Several people wrote brief comments on the sheet.
Mira stood near the front table, hands folded loosely.
Hana watched someone pause in front of the central watercolor display.
The room remained calm.
The rain outside softened the window light.
The finished artwork gave the old classroom a gentle sense of purpose.
At least, that was how it looked.
Mira looked at her notebook one last time.
Every box on the checklist had been marked.
They shared a small laugh, quiet enough not to disturb the room.
When the last visitor left, Theo glanced at the comment sheet.
Hana leaned closer.
The handwriting was faint and narrow.
Mira read the next line silently.
Please do not move the tables again.
She blinked.
When Theo looked again, the comment seemed shorter.
Only one line remained.
The room feels peaceful.
Mira closed the notebook.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: The comment sheet is being used.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Backup pen was unnecessary, but still wise.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: The spacing works. Nothing feels crowded.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: We finished on time.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: And without moving the same table six times.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: Only twice.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Someone wrote that the room feels peaceful.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Let’s clean up.

actions: Visitors quietly preview the exhibition.
Several comments are written on the comment sheet.
Theo reads a peaceful comment aloud.
Mira silently sees an additional line asking not to move the tables again.
The comment appears shorter when Theo looks again.
Mira closes the notebook and decides to clean up.

narration: After the preview ended, the three cleaned up the extra supplies.
The unused tape, spare cards, and empty boxes were returned to the art club room.
The frames and artwork stayed in the old classroom for the next day.
The hallway lights had turned warmer as evening approached.
The wall clock showed that they had finished with time to spare.
Theo carried the empty box under one arm.
Hana held her folder against her chest.
Mira closed the blue notebook and placed it in her tote bag.
They walked toward the school gate together.
Outside, the rain had slowed to a fine mist.
The ground reflected the soft evening light.
At the gate, they paused for a moment.
Mira looked back at the building.
One window on the upper floor reflected the pale sky.
The old classroom window did not.
The three said goodbye and headed home in different directions.
The day had been ordinary, steady, and productive.
Their work was finished, and the exhibition would be ready in the morning.
Behind them, the school gate stood still.
From somewhere inside the building, too faint to be certain, a clock continued to tick.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Today went smoothly.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: It helped that everyone had a role.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Tomorrow, we only need to open the room and make sure the pens are there.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Both pens.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: Both pens.

dialogue.speaker: Hana
dialogue.text: The classroom looked different after everything was arranged.

dialogue.speaker: Theo
dialogue.text: Still a classroom, but more welcoming.

dialogue.speaker: Mira
dialogue.text: That is enough for a small exhibition.

actions: The group cleans up extra supplies after the preview.
They return unused materials to the art club room.
They walk through the hallway and toward the school gate.
At the gate, Mira looks back at the building.
The old classroom window does not reflect the sky.
The three friends say goodbye and head home.
